title: Stieglitz, Steichen, Strand: Masterworks from The Metropolitan Museum of Art

publisher.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art / Yale University Press

description.main: Catalogue of the 2010-11 Metropolitan Museum exhibition of its Stieglitz, Steichen and Strand holdings, by Malcolm Daniel.
description.extended:
Catalogue of the Metropolitan Museum's first exhibition of its holdings by three founding figures of American photographic modernism: Alfred Stieglitz, Edward Steichen and Paul Strand.

Malcolm Daniel's volume accompanied the show at the Met, November 10, 2010 to April 10, 2011. Stieglitz appears through portraits, landscapes, city views and cloud studies, including photographs from his composite portrait of Georgia O'Keeffe, chosen by O'Keeffe herself for the museum. Steichen is represented by three large variant prints of The Flatiron and his moonlit photographs of Rodin's Balzac. The Strand section draws on the 1915-16 work published in the last double issue of Camera Work: movement in the city, abstractions and street portraits, shown in rare large platinum prints.

Stieglitz (1864-1946) promoted photography through the Little Galleries of the Photo-Secession, known as 291, and through the journal Camera Work. Steichen (1879-1973) was his collaborator in Paris and later a fashion and celebrity photographer and a curator at the Museum of Modern Art. Strand (1890-1976) moved photography from soft-focus Pictorialism toward the straight approach.
